subject: How many samples recommended for establishing new trained set?

messages.author: e7f0f6d405df3839
messages.subject: How many samples recommended for establishing new trained set?
parts:
The paper seems to indicate that at least 60 replicates are recommended for a new training set. I just would like to confirm that I am interpreting that properly. What aspects of performance seem to decrease with fewer than that number? If the input arrays for training have very high correlation/low sample-sample variance would fewer arrays be required for adequate classifier performance?
Thanks!

messages.author: cad36eead1754edc
messages.subject: Re: How many samples recommended for establishing new trained set?
parts:
Hi,

The 60 arrays refers to the minimum needed for decent GRN reconstruction, and this relies on sampling from a range of perturbations to the network (and therefore a relatively higher overall sample-sample variance). We got this number from Faith et al. 2007. Once you have a GRN, training the classifier can be done with fewer than 60 profiles, and in fact we did this for some of the Illumina arrays. In my opinion, the most important aspect is to have independent samples that you can use to assess the performance of the classifier.

Hope this helps, and please let me know if you have any more questions.

Best,

Patrick
